questions.question: Which command-line tool lets AI coding agents search and install Gemini agent skills from the google-gemini/gemini-skills repository?
questions.expected_answer: Use skills.sh (`npx skills add google-gemini/gemini-skills --list` or `--skill <skill-name> --global`) or Context7 (`npx ctx7 skills install /google-gemini/gemini-skills <skill-name>`).
questions.evidence_quote: npx skills add google-gemini/gemini-skills --list

questions.question: What happens to the Gemini API CLI (`gemini-api`) output when you pass `--dry-run`?
questions.expected_answer: `--dry-run` validates inputs, redacts credentials, and previews the HTTP request offline.
questions.evidence_quote: `--dry-run` validates inputs, redacts credentials, and previews the HTTP request offline.

questions.question: Starting May 28, 2026, what kind of API keys are created by default in Google AI Studio, and what happens to unrestricted standard keys?
questions.expected_answer: All new API keys are automatically created as authorization (auth) keys, and the Gemini API rejects requests from unrestricted standard keys.
questions.evidence_quote:
Starting May 28, 2026, all new API keys created in
  Google AI Studio are automatically created as auth keys.

questions.question: In the models_and_pricing section, what is the context window and introductory 1M-token price for Gemini 4 Carbon?
questions.expected_answer: Gemini 4 Carbon has a 1M unified tokens context window and an introductory price of $2.00 / $10.00 per 1M tokens through Nov 30.
questions.evidence_quote: *   *Price (1M)* **$2.00 / $10.00 (intro thru Nov 30)**

questions.question: Which model should developers migrate to now that Veo 3.1 Preview has been shut down in the Gemini API?
questions.expected_answer: Developers should migrate to Gemini Omni Flash (`gemini-omni-1.2-flash`) or the GA models available through the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.
questions.evidence_quote:
Use [Gemini Omni Flash](/docs/omni) (`gemini-omni-1.2-flash`) as your model for
video generation and conversational video editing in the Gemini API.

questions.question: In Gemini 4 models, how does the API behave if your input tokens plus `max_output_tokens` exceed 1,048,576 tokens?
questions.expected_answer: The API automatically caps the output limit to the remaining space in the context window (1,048,576 minus your input tokens).
questions.evidence_quote: If your input tokens plus `max_output_tokens` exceed 1,048,576 tokens, the API automatically caps the output limit to the remaining space in the context window (`1,048,576` minus your input tokens).

questions.question: What are the two fields contained in every `thought` step returned by the Interactions API?
questions.expected_answer: Every `thought` step contains `signature` (required) and `summary` (optional).
questions.evidence_quote: An encrypted representation of the model's internal reasoning state. Always present, even when the model performs minimal reasoning.

questions.question: How does the Paid tier of the Gemini Developer API differ from the Free tier regarding user content privacy and batch processing?
questions.expected_answer: In the Paid tier, content is not used to improve Google's products, and users get access to Context caching and the Batch API (50% cost reduction).
questions.evidence_quote: Content **not** used to improve our products

questions.question: In the tools_and_agents section, how should managed agents store and use external secrets without exposing them inside the sandbox?
questions.expected_answer: Store secrets as managed credentials and reference them by ID so the egress proxy injects them at request time and they are never exposed inside the sandbox.
questions.evidence_quote:
Store
secrets as managed credentials and reference them by ID, so the egress proxy
injects them at request time and they are never exposed inside the sandbox.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code and error code are returned when your Prepay credit balance is depleted?
questions.expected_answer: HTTP 402 Payment Required with the error code `payment_required`.
questions.evidence_quote: | `payment_required` | 402 Payment Required | Your Prepay credit balance is depleted.

questions.question: Which libraries do the Google GenAI SDKs support for defining Structured Outputs schemas in Python and JavaScript?
questions.expected_answer: They allow defining schemas using Pydantic in Python and Zod in JavaScript, in addition to JSON Schema in the REST API.
questions.evidence_quote:
In addition to supporting JSON Schema in the REST API, the Google GenAI SDKs
allow defining schemas using
[Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/) (Python) and
[Zod](https://zod.dev/) (JavaScript).

questions.question: Up to how many pages can Gemini models process in a PDF document using native vision?
questions.expected_answer: Up to 1000 pages.
questions.evidence_quote:
Analyze and interpret content, including text, images, diagrams,
  charts, and tables, even in long documents up to 1000 pages.

questions.question: In the getting_started section, which transport protocol and SDK method are used to open a Gemini Live API session?
questions.expected_answer: The Gemini Live API uses WebSockets and is opened asynchronously via `client.aio.live.connect(model=model, config=config)`.
questions.evidence_quote: The Gemini Live API uses WebSockets for real-time communication.

questions.question: Which API version do the latest Google Gen AI SDKs default to starting November 2026, and what happens if you call a v1beta-only feature without changing it?
questions.expected_answer: They default to `v1`, and calls to `v1beta`-only features (such as Live API, explicit context caching, or managed agents) fail until you set the API version to `v1beta`.
questions.evidence_quote:
Starting with the November 2026 major
  releases, the Google Gen AI SDKs call `v1` unless you set a version.

questions.question: Which Gemini 4 model is described as fast and efficient for everyday coding and agentic workflows, and what is its 1M-token price?
questions.expected_answer: Gemini 4 Hydrogen (`gemini-4-hydrogen`), priced at $1.50 / $7.50 per 1M tokens.
questions.evidence_quote:
*   *Model ID* **`gemini-4-hydrogen`**
  *   *Price (1M)* **$1.50 / $7.50**

questions.question: In the api_reference section, what is the difference between `rate_limit_exceeded` and `quota_exceeded` error codes?
questions.expected_answer: Both return HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, but `rate_limit_exceeded` means exceeding per-minute/per-second request or token limits (retry with exponential backoff), while `quota_exceeded` means exceeding the daily quota (wait for reset or request an increase).
questions.evidence_quote: | `quota_exceeded` | 429 Too Many Requests | You have exceeded your daily quota.

questions.question: How are non-PDF text formats like TXT, Markdown, or HTML handled by Gemini compared to PDF files?
questions.expected_answer: Non-PDF documents such as TXT, Markdown, or HTML are processed as plain text, which eliminates visual context like charts or formatting.
questions.evidence_quote:
Other non-PDF documents, such as TXT, Markdown, or HTML files, are processed as
plain text, which eliminates context like charts or formatting.

questions.question: What happens if your coding agent does not have the Gemini Docs MCP server installed when using a Gemini agent skill?
questions.expected_answer: The skill falls back to `llms.txt` (`https://aistudio.google.com/llms.txt`).
questions.evidence_quote: If your agent does not have the MCP server installed, the skill falls back to [`llms.txt`](https://aistudio.google.com/llms.txt).

questions.question: In the tools_and_agents section, what is the default outbound network access policy for managed agents in their Linux sandbox, and how can you restrict it?
questions.expected_answer: By default, environments have unrestricted outbound network access; you can restrict outbound traffic to specific domains or wildcard patterns using a `network` allowlist.
questions.evidence_quote:
By default, environments have unrestricted outbound network access. Use a
`network` allowlist to restrict outbound traffic to specific domains or
wildcard patterns.
